newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-London coffee due up $50-60, seen sideways.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-London coffee due up $50-60, seen sideways.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
London traders are expecting an opening rise in coffee futures.
Analysts question whether the market can manage the momentum to sustain an upmove. They expect the market to range sideways in the short term.
Traders said the market was due to open around $50-60 higher.
London traders rejected calls by South East Asian traders for LIFFE coffee to open $150 or more down. Such a call could not be reconciled with New York's performance on Tuesday, London traders said.

On a technical basis, coffee was likely to range sideways, Susan Rigg, technical analyst at Chart Analysis, said. She noted that it had moved above the $1,800 level. Rigg described the market as shell-shocked after its recent sharp falls, a factor which militated against a sharp rise. "If it moves above $2,000 it will look a lot better," she said.
The market was supported below $1,700, she said, and then down to $1,500.
New York coffee futures ended mixed Tuesday in local-dominated trading, dealers said.
Traders said activity was extremely dull, with an estimated 6,130 lots changing hands.
While the lack of a cold threat in Brazil might limit the market's upside potential for now, New York traders said dwindling exchange certified coffee stocks provided underlying support.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 250 60-kg bags as of June 23 to 46,175 bags. There were 9,512 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
